description: Tab strip component with Line, Pill, and Enclosed visual variants. Supports icons, badges, disabled tabs, and keyboard arrow-key navigation. Use with TmTabPanel children.

parameters.name: ActiveTabId
parameters.description: ID of the currently active tab.

parameters.name: ActiveTabIdChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the active tab changes.

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: Visual variant of the tab strip.

parameters.name: Wrap
parameters.description: When true, the tab strip wraps onto multiple rows to fit the available width instead of scrolling horizontally. Use when many tabs would otherwise overflow/truncate in a narrow container.

parameters.name: HeaderLeading
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately BEFORE the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it. The tab strip owns a roving tabindex (Arrow/Home/End, tabindex 0/-1, aria-selected AND the DOM focus, which moves with the selection); an element that can never be selected would misreport that contract to assistive technology and would be reachable with the arrow keys as if it were a tab. Setting this (or HeaderTrailing) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all, so existing CSS and tests that rely on .tm-tabs > .tm-tabs__header keep working. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, a sticky tab strip must stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header). Sticking the header alone pins only the strip and lets the slot content scroll away.

parameters.name: HeaderTrailing
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately AFTER the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it, for the same roving-focus reason as HeaderLeading. Setting this (or HeaderLeading) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header), otherwise the slot content scrolls away from under the pinned strip.
